problem: VLMs lack persistent, queryable memory of the physical world; existing RAG and spatio-temporal memory methods rely on static corpora, short contexts or pre-collected data and do not retrieve jointly over semantic, spatial and temporal axes, nor share memory across agents.
motivation: Humans build persistent what/where/when mental representations that let them recall past events and infer unobserved states. Embodied agents need the same lifelong, metric-anchored memory to answer long-horizon episodic questions without retraining the VLM.
key_idea: Continuously build an object-level 4D knowledge database (semantic text embeddings, SLAM-anchored 3D positions, temporal intervals) and let a frozen VLM decompose queries into semantic/spatial/temporal keys to iteratively retrieve from it.
insight: Single retrieval keys give only modest gains (best +6.4 points over no memory in the ablation), while semantic+spatial gives 74.7 and all three give 78.6 on EM-EQA vs 49.8 without memory, so the axes are complementary. Spatial and temporal cues without semantics (A7) help little, so VLM semantics are the anchor. A shared multi-agent memory improved A-EQA SPL from 61.47 to 70.13, showing the global metric frame enables efficient reuse of others' observations.
method: 4D object feature generation: SAM2 masks each frame, projects point clouds onto masks to get 3D centroid and extent, and the VLM writes a concise semantic description; the entry is {SEM, SPA, TEM} plus timestamp.

Triple storage: SEM is embedded in a vector DB, SPA sits in a global metric 3D space via special points in a MapAnything SLAM map, TEM is in a columnar time-series DB with appearance and disappearance times.
Continuous update: a new object is matched to existing entries by centroid distance < eps_c and embedding cosine similarity > delta_s; the VLM decides whether to merge/refine or insert a new entry.
Collaborative enrichment: multiple agents align SLAM maps into a shared global frame and write into/read from one common database.
Self-estimated answerability: the VLM answers from live perception if confident, otherwise it triggers retrieval.

4D retrieval: the VLM derives semantic, spatial and temporal keys, retrieved by cosine similarity, nearest-neighbour/directional filtering on the map, and interval search respectively; queries can be chained.
Context construction and reasoning loop: retrieved records are serialized into text C(q) and appended to the query, a = VLM(q ⊕ C(q)), iterating until termination.

setting.backbone: Gemma3-4B-IT (frozen) with SAM2 Hiera-Large and MapAnything
setting.observation: RGB images + point clouds/depth with timestamps and SLAM poses (MapAnything)
setting.action_space: exploration in A-EQA; no low-level action space described
setting.simulator: OpenEQA (ScanNet, HM3D); ERQA and VLM4D are offline datasets

numbers.extra: training-free; memory built from the provided images
five auxiliary agents populate shared 4D memory; single-agent variant gives 72.82 / 61.47

numbers.eval_set_note: cross-conditioned: memory built from the other half of the benchmark
numbers.extra: benchmark split into two halves; memory from one half used to answer the other

numbers_note: Benchmarks are EQA rather than navigation; split labels for OpenEQA and the others are not stated in the paper and 'val'/'test' are best guesses. The ablation table (Table 5) reports 78.6 for the full model on a 184-question EM-EQA subset, not the main-table 79.77.
results: With a frozen 4B VLM, R4 gets 70.25 on ERQA (vs GPT-5 65.7), 79.77 on OpenEQA EM-EQA (vs GPT-5 64.4) and 74.00 / 63.37 on A-EQA HM3D (vs 3D-Mem 52.6 / 42.0). It reaches 77.31 overall on cross-conditioned VLM4D (vs Gemini-2.5-Pro 62.0). Shared memory adds +8.66 SPL on A-EQA.
limitations: Storage and retrieval latency limits real-time and multi-agent deployment.

No existing benchmark evaluates collaboration through shared SLAM maps, so the collaborative claim is only tested on a 184-task A-EQA subset; the memory does not encode intrinsic object motion (weak on ERQA 'other' at 42.86).
Evaluation is on QA benchmarks only, with no real-robot or closed-loop navigation experiments; the VLM4D setup is a custom adaptation.
